contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer who knows calculus, complex numbers and constant-coefficient linear ODEs and is starting control theory
contract.problem: Acquiring the vocabulary and performance measures the later entries use, and knowing where the textbook step-response formulas come from and when they hold
contract.outcome: Name the loop roles and the four requirements and why they trade off; define LTI systems, the Laplace transform, transfer function, poles, zeros and steady-state gain; read a step response; derive the second-order overshoot formula and see why 4/(zeta wn) is only an estimate
contract.contribution: Both benchmark formulas derived on the page, the settling-time estimate tested against the exact response for four damping ratios, and a standard-library script that reproduces the numbers
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; one Python script with quoted output; Astrom and Murray (2021); Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini (2019); Ogata (2010)
contract.limitations: Second-order benchmark only; no frequency response or controller design; limits of the measures stated qualitatively

findings.location: Section 3.3 plant equation and Section 4.2 pole pair (360 px; mobile-light-09, 14)
findings.problem: Both displays are wider than the column; b > 0 and the end of the definition of omega_d are hidden behind an unmarked sideways scroll
findings.whyItMatters: The 4.2 display is the only definition of omega_d, which 4.3 and 4.4 use
findings.action: Put the two parts of each display on separate lines, or add a site-level scroll cue for wide equations

findings.problem: Only three columns are visible; the exact settling time column is beyond the scroll shadow
findings.whyItMatters: The table exists to compare the estimate with the exact value

findings.location: Section 1.2 loop diagram and Section 4.2 step-response plot (360 px; mobile-light-05, 14, 15)
